body: With the current implementation of the `no-unused-expressions` rule, directives should _always_ generate the error "Expected an assignment or function call and instead saw an expression". @nzakas: Do you want us to ignore strings in directive position until a real `DirectiveStatement` node is added in esprima?

I see the same problem as @MichaelPaulukonis with eslint 0.1.0 (the one published on npm) but can't reproduce the error with 0.2.0-dev (from github).  Any chance that 0.2.0 will be pushed to npm soon?

@michaelficarra I think we need to special-case "use strict" in a directive position (I wouldn't generically say that for all strings)

@smikes 0.2.0 still has a lot of tickets open before it can be pushed.

issue.body:
> A Use Strict Directive is an _ExpressionStatement_ in a Directive Prologue whose _StringLiteral_ is either the exact character sequences **"use strict"** or **'use strict'**. A Use Strict Directive may not contain an _EscapeSequence_ or _LineContinuation_.

http://www.ecma-international.org/ecma-262/5.1/#sec-14.1

Currently it treats `'use strict'` as an unexpected expression.
